sub_indicators.label: Cybercrime and cybersecurity law
sub_indicators.subject: gov.legislate
sub_indicators.text: Cybersecurity legislation: cybercrime and cybersecurity law
sub_indicators.norm_short: The Malabo Convention commits each party to legal measures against cybercrime: Article 25 on legislation and Articles 29 to 31 on the offences. It sets no test of whether a law is used.
criteria: A source from the past three years says the country has no cybercrime or cybersecurity law and no bill for one.
A cybercrime or cybersecurity bill is drafted, before parliament or passed. No law is known to be in force.
A cybercrime or cybersecurity law is in force, as an act of its own or as part of a penal or digital code. No use of it is on record in the past three years.
The law has been used in the past three years: a dated arrest, charge, prosecution or conviction, or a penalty from the body it sets up. Who it was used against is not judged.
The law is in regular use: sources from the past two years show it used again and again, judged case by case. Two or three cases are not regular use.
